question: Following the irresponsible decision by Berlin’s ‘traffic light’ coalition, tolerated by the Commission, to decriminalise cannabis consumption, drug smuggling by mafia gangs across the Mediterranean from Morocco to southern Spain risks spiralling out of control once and for all. The local customs authorities appear to be completely swamped by organised crime. 1.
Is the Commission willing to consider extending Frontex's mandate, which remains wholly inadequate to address irregular migration, to encompass at least drug smuggling?
When can we expect to see a proposal in this regard?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.6.

2024) The findings of the Commission’s recent evaluation of the European Border and Coast Guard (EBCG) Regulation and the review of the Standing Corps1, have confirmed that the mandate of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) is appropriate to address the current and future challenges at the EU’s external borders as concerns the cross-border movement of persons.
Its current mandate already enables Frontex to provide support to the Member States, Europol, and Eurojust, in the fight against serious cross-border crime2.

Frontex’s involvement in various activities under the umbrella of the European Multidisciplinary Platform Against Criminal Threats (EMPACT) also demonstrates the Agency’s contribution to the EU’s efforts to prevent and counter cross-border crime, including drug trafficking. The Commission will continue closely following the ongoing implementation of the EBCG Regulation.

The Commission also engages in regular Security Dialogues with Morocco to address, amongst other matters, the issue of drug smuggling. It is however important to note that managing the cross-border flow of goods and performing risk management on goods crossing the EU external border to target suspicious consignments falls under the sole competence of the customs authorities and is not part of the mandate of Frontex.

The Commission has last year tabled an ambitious reform of the Customs Union which includes the creation of an EU Customs Authority, a new decentralised agency, which would perform inter alia EU level risk management activities on goods entering and leaving the EU to support the national customs authorities and ensure a more harmonized application of customs controls.
It is envisaged that the EU Customs Authority would closely cooperate with Europol and Frontex in the future.
1 Report from the Commission to the European parliament and the Council on the evaluation of Regulation (EU)

2019/1896 on the European Border and Coast Guard, including a review of the Standing Corps, COM(2024)75 final, 02.02.2024. 2 Regulation (EU) 2019/1896 on the European Border and Coast Guard, Article 10(1)(q).
